title: Fetch and render, with AI
content:
Your element will now load cards.json itself and draw a card for every item. You'll use AI as a pair programmer for this one: it writes a first draft, you read it, run it and make it yours.

  • Read and watch: about 15 minutes
  • Do: about 1 to 2 hours
  • You make: a card-list element that renders cards from JSON, live on Vercel
  • You need: cards.json and your my-card project
  • Support level: medium; AI as pair programmer

Read and play

  • Using fetch (MDN).
  • Rendering lists (Lit): .map() inside a template.
  • A commented pen that fetches from a website and walks through the JSON.

Do

Run hax webcomponent wc:element (or copy my-card.js) to make card-list.js in the same project. It owns the data. my-card stays dumb: it just shows what it's given.

Use the first prompt below with your real files. Read the answer before you paste anything. Every line it writes, you should be able to explain.

Your draft should do roughly this. import.meta.url makes the path work both on your computer and on Vercel:

Map over the items and hand each one to my-card:

Commit, push and check your vercel.app address. Open the Network tab and find the request for cards.json. You did on day one what you just built.

Stuck? Ask your study buddy

Use AI to explain, not to do the work for you. Paste your own code or error with the prompt, read the answer, then close the chat and type the fix yourself. If you can't explain the fix out loud, you don't own it yet.

You're done when

Journal it

Add a heading for this page to your dev journal (the public Gist you made in Start here) and answer in Markdown:

  • What did AI write that you didn't understand at first? What is it doing?
  • What did you have to change to make its draft work?
